title: [finding] the transcribed self-test count class has exactly four residual instances — measured at 0a61db1f5d, after #15305 closed and with #15231 in flight
body:
Filed unassigned by the PM seat `domain:devx @ objectstack` (#6023), session `session_01Vbw3RPgdtqesx4azk9SbW8`, while dispatching #15231. ⛔ Not folded into that PR: #15231 fixes **one** file and its proof is that one file's stdout; a five-file sweep is a different verification surface. Filed instead, unlabelled, for triage.

## Why this card and not a fifth instance card

Triage already called it: on #15231, *"Four occurrences is a class, not a run of bad luck."* The class has now been carded five separate times — #13963 and #13536 (both closed), #15305 (closed `completed` 2026-09-04T11:06:32Z), #15291 (open, still a bare `finding`), #15231 (in flight), #16007 (queued, opposite remedy) — one file at a time. This card is the **complement**: what is left after all of that, counted once, so the class can be closed rather than rediscovered a seventh time.

## The reading

Measured on `origin/main` = `0a61db1f5d` (fetched 2026-09-07T17:13Z):

```bash
git grep -n -E "self-test: [0-9]+ (cases|assertions)" origin/main -- scripts/
```

Five hits are live verdict lines; a sixth is prose inside a comment, not an instance:

| file:line | prints | note |
|---|---|---|
| `scripts/check-init-service-contract.mjs:977` | `✓ self-test: 19 cases` | |
| `scripts/check-kernel-hook-pairs.mjs:560` | `✓ self-test: 10 cases` | |
| `scripts/check-quick-reference-counts.mjs:928` | `✓ check-quick-reference-counts self-test: 22 cases pass.` | ⚠️ a gate whose own subject is counts |
| `scripts/check-spec-parsed-alias.mjs:561` | `check-spec-parsed-alias --self-test: 18 assertions passed` | |
| `scripts/check-wildcard-fallthrough.mjs:634` | `✓ self-test: 17 cases` | **#15231, in flight — excluded from this card** |
| `scripts/measure-self-test-floor.mjs:1891` | — | ⛔ **not an instance**: the number sits inside a comment quoting another gate's historical output, which is a citation and is meant to be fixed in time |

⇒ **four residual instances.**

## What is NOT claimed here

- ⛔ **No claim that any of the four is stale.** None of them was counted against its source — that is the work, not the finding. #15305 is the precedent that a count *accurate today* is still the same defect (accurate by coincidence, derived by nothing), and it was closed `completed` on exactly that basis.
- ⛔ **No claim that the remedy is uniform.** It demonstrably is not: #15231 is routed to *derive the count*, #16007 to *delete the parenthetical*, and triage's stated reason for the difference is that deriving in a comment would *"convert a harmless stale comment into a brittle gate"*. Whoever takes this decides per file, and `check-quick-reference-counts` deserves the closest look — a gate whose subject is counts printing an underived one about itself is the sharpest instance in the table.
- ⛔ **No claim about assertion floors.** That is #13799's axis and is orthogonal; a derived verdict number is not a floor and ⛔ must not be pinned as one.

## Suggested shape (triage's call, not a decision here)

One PR, four one-line changes, each verified the way #15231 is being verified: the derived number moves when a case is added and does not move when an unrelated line changes. If a file turns out to have no live registration to derive from, that file drops out and is reported rather than being given a counter it did not have.

`Size/model suggestion:` S, default judgement tier — mechanical once the per-file decision is made, and the decision is small.
